name: Roing
description: District headquarters of Lower Dibang Valley, a scenic plain town at the foothills of the Mishmi Hills serving as the main base for exploring the region's lakes, wildlife, forts, and hill passes. Known for orange orchards and as a commercial hub for the area.
facts: Headquarters of Lower Dibang Valley district
Population around 11,389 as per 2011 census
Base for visits to Mehao Lake, Mayodia Pass, and Bhishmaknagar Fort
Home to Idu Mishmi and Adi communities; Reh festival celebrated in February

name: Mehao Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Protected area of 281.5 sq km established in 1980 around Mehao Lake, featuring virgin tropical evergreen to temperate forests rich in orchids, birds, and rare mammals including clouded leopards, red pandas, and Mishmi takin.
facts: Area 281.5 km²; altitude range 400–3,560 m
Home to over 200 bird species, rare orchids, and endemic Mishmi Hills hoolock gibbon subspecies
Includes Mehao Lake and parts of Dibang Wildlife Sanctuary influences
Best visited October to March; about 17 km from Roing

name: Mehao Lake
description: Crystal-clear natural lake covering about 4 sq km at around 3,000 feet elevation inside Mehao Wildlife Sanctuary, 14 km from Roing. Attracts seasonal birds and wild ducks; low-nutrient oligotrophic waters with no fish, ideal for trekking and photography.
facts: Located 14 km from Roing at approximately 900–1,000 m elevation
Crystal clear waters attracting wild ducks; classified as oligotrophic
Surrounded by dense virgin forest rich in flora and fauna
Popular for short treks through the sanctuary forest

name: Sally Lake
description: Serene lake resort just 3–4 km from Roing amidst lush forest, overlooking the Dibang River valley. Ideal for picnics, with clear waters hosting fish and a tourist lodge nearby.
facts: Located 3.8 km from Roing town
Overlooks Dibang River and surrounding valley
Popular day-trip and picnic spot with tourist lodge
Part of the broader Mehao landscape near the wildlife sanctuary

name: Nehru Van Udyan
description: Beautiful forest park barely 1 km from Roing on the bank of the Deopani (Eje) River, featuring maintained gardens, orchid and cactus houses, and the Eje-Breeze Tower overlooking the river confluence.
facts: Located about 1 km from Roing Township
Features orchid and cactus houses plus guest facilities
Near the confluence of Eje and Eme rivers, ideal for picnics
Also known as a place where only nature speaks

name: Mipi Pene Centre
description: Cultural centre at Ezenggo, Roing, dedicated to preserving and promoting the Igu (shaman) system and traditions of the Idu Mishmi community. Established in 2017, it includes a museum, seminar hall, and learning facilities.
facts: Located at Ezenggo, Roing
Established in 2017; inaugurated in 2018 by CM Pema Khandu
Preserves Igu shamanic traditions and Idu Mishmi culture
Includes museum, auditorium, and dormitory for scholars

name: RIWATCH
description: Research Institute of World and Ancient Traditions and Cultures and Heritage, an institute-cum-museum near Abali Village about 15 km from Roing, attracting students and researchers interested in local traditions.
facts: Located near Abali Village, about 15 km from Roing
Institute-cum-museum focused on ancient traditions and cultures
Visited by foreign students and researchers
Supports documentation of regional heritage

name: Dambuk
description: Emerging tourism town known for orange orchards and the annual Orange Festival of Adventure and Music, featuring adventure sports, cultural shows, and live music against paddy fields and orchards.
facts: Hosts the annual Orange Festival of Adventure and Music since around 2015
Surrounded by orange orchards and paddy fields
Emerging destination for adventure and cultural tourism
Accessible from Roing within the district

name: Jia Hot Spring
description: Natural hot spring at Jia village offering a serene spot for bathing and observing local village life, located about 19 minutes' drive from Roing.
facts: Located at Jia village, approximately 19 minutes from Roing
Provides rejuvenating hot-spring baths
Opportunity to experience daily village life of local communities
Peaceful natural setting in the foothills

name: Bhishmaknagar Fort
description: Ancient archaeological site and fort ruins about 30 km southeast of Roing, linked to the Chutia Kingdom (11th–16th centuries) and local legends involving Rukmini from the Mahabharata. Features brick structures, gates, and ramparts.
facts: Located about 30 km from Roing in Lower Dibang Valley
Ruins dated to 8th–15th centuries; associated with Chutia Kingdom
Spread over large area with brick plinths, gates, and rampart walls
Identified with historical Sadhayapuri; excavated in 1965–70

name: Mayodia Pass
description: High mountain pass at 2,655 m elevation, 56 km from Roing, famous for winter snowfall (November–March) and panoramic views of the valley. Offers trekking, wildlife sightings including Mishmi takin, and a guest house.
facts: Elevation 2,655 metres (8,711 ft); 56 km from Roing
Experiences snowfall from November to March, heaviest in January–February
Name derived from Deori-Chutia or Idu-Mishmi words meaning related to mother goddess or Mayu peak
Gateway towards Hunli and higher reaches; wildlife including flying squirrels and takin

name: Iphipani
description: Scenic picnic spot about 10 km from Roing offering views of the Dibang River plain valley, suitable for angling, cooking by the riverbank, and enjoying the natural setting.
facts: Located 10 km from Roing Township
Provides picturesque views of the Dibang River valley
Ideal for picnics, fishing, and riverside relaxation
Also known as Iphi-pani ghat

name: Nijomaghat
description: Historical picnic spot 15 km from Roing, established by the British in the 19th century and named after political officer J.F. Needham. Features river views between mountains and a ferry connection.
facts: Located 15 km from Roing
Named after British Political Officer J.F. Needham
Former access point into the hills during colonial period
Scenic river and mountain views; small ferry to Dambuk area

name: Hunli
description: Picturesque sub-divisional headquarters town at about 1,500 m elevation, 90 km from Roing via Mayodia Pass. Known for scenic valley views, circuit house, and nearby cave temple at Kupunli.
facts: Sub-divisional headquarters at approximately 5,000 feet elevation
About 90 km drive from Roing crossing Mayodia Pass
Nearby Cave Temple of Kupunli (about 2 hours trek)
Offers splendid valley views from the ridge

name: Ita and Padum Pukhuri
description: Historical brick-built ponds at Ithili village about 14 km from Roing. Padum Pukhuri is known for blooming lotus flowers in October/November.
facts: Located at Ithili village, about 14 km from Roing
Historical brick-built ponds
Padum Pukhuri features lotus blooms in October/November
Part of the local historical and natural attractions
